evidence: Carborundum Aquatint // September: Carborundum aquatint is a painterly intaglio process whereby the various strengths of a brushmark are determined by the use of fine or coarse carborundum grit mixed in suspension with acrylic matte or gloss medium. Participants will use chip board, matt board, and plexiglass for the printing plates. Students will create an edition from a single plate as well as an edition from a multi plate image where registration is explained.
Tags: Visual Arts, Art, Workshop, Education, Printmaking, Participatory, Format, Aquatint
prioritized.existing_alternative: Paintbrush alone implies painting; printer suggests digital output, and generic printmaking may omit the named technique.
prioritized.label: Carborundum aquatint
prioritized.rationale: The workshop explicitly uses grit-based intaglio plates; surface texture and plate-to-paper process distinguish it from painting. Fine texture must be simplified and tested.
prioritized.visual: A brush depositing a broad gritty patch on an inked plate beside a clean pulled paper corner.
prioritized.priority_rationale: Valuable rare technique; test a gritty plate and pulled print before choosing this over broader intaglio artwork.
